root_cause.text: The ct_vm_map() function always accesses PTEs from only vm->ptp[0].area regardless of the CT_PTP_NUM value, causing out-of-bounds memory access when CT_PTP_NUM was increased to 4 without refactoring the virtual memory allocation logic to distribute PTEs across multiple page table pages.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states "ct_vm_map() always uses PTEs in vm->ptp[0].area regardless of CT_PTP_NUM" and notes that "On AMD64 systems, a single PTP covers 512 PTEs (2M). When aggregate memory allocations exceed this limit, ct_vm_map() tries to access beyond the allocated space and causes a page fault." The patch reverts CT_PTP_NUM from 4 back to 1, confirming that the mismatch between the declared number of page table pages (4) and the actual implementation (which only uses the first one) was the root cause of the vulnerability.

vuln_statements.stmt_text: #define CT_PTP_NUM	4	/* num of device page table pages */
vuln_statements.explanation: This macro definition declares CT_PTP_NUM as 4, indicating 4 page table pages should be used. However, the ct_vm_map() function implementation only accesses PTEs from vm->ptp[0].area regardless of this CT_PTP_NUM value. This mismatch between the declared constant (4) and the actual implementation (which only uses index 0) is the root cause of the out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability. The code allocates memory for 4 page table pages but only uses the first one, causing PTEs that should be distributed across multiple pages to overflow the first page's bounds.
